resale_co.name: Construction Records Clearance (CRC)
resale_co.issued_by: Readington Township Construction Code Office (enforcing agency)
resale_co.lead_time: Code says to apply with the fee at least 10 business days before the change of ownership or occupancy; the fee is lower when filed 6 to 12 business days ahead.
resale_co.valid_for: 6 months from the date of issue, unless a change in occupancy has occurred
requirements: Records check by the construction office: no open construction permits on the property
Any open permits must get final inspections and the proper Uniform Construction Code certificates before the CRC is issued
Exempt transfers (for example spouse to spouse, parent and child, estate distribution, refinancing, deed corrections) do not need a CRC as long as no change in physical occupancy occurs

fees.label: Construction Records Clearance, 6 to 12 business days
Construction Records Clearance, 1 to 5 business days

resale_co.how_to_apply: Submit the Application for Construction Records Clearance (seller name, property address, block and lot, closing date, residential or commercial) with the fee to the Readington Township Code Enforcement / Construction office, 509 Route 523, Whitehouse Station, or use the Township's online CRC submission form linked on the Construction page. Choose pick-up or mail to owner/agent.
resale_co.contact_title: Construction Official (Code Office / Technical Assistant Kristina Chin, ext. 244)

evidence.quote: A construction records clearance (CRC) shall be required prior to the sale of any residential or commercial structure.

The owner or his authorized agent shall submit a written application and payment of fees at least 10 business days prior to the change of ownership and/or occupancy on the form provided by the Township.
Prior to the issuance of any such certificate for any transaction, the enforcing agency shall conduct a records inspection to ensure that there are no open construction permits on subject premises.
One to five business days: $70.
Six to 12 business days: $40.
Certificates are valid for six months from the date of issue unless a change in occupancy has occurred, and must be renewed for each occupancy change.
Application for Construction Records Clearance
Construction Record Clearance (CRC) – Online Submission
Thomas Petto Construction Official
is required for any change in use or in tenant for an existing non-residential space or building.

resale_co.notes: Readington does not do a physical resale inspection. Its sale requirement is a Construction Records Clearance under Code Section 96-6 (added October 15, 2012, Ord. No. 22-2012, read through the ecode360 print view), which checks for open permits. The posted form is a scanned 2017 PDF with the same $40 / $70 fees as the code. The online CRC submission link on the Construction page points to a Google Form. The Zoning Certificate of Continual Occupancy ($100) is only for non-residential space. Construction staff emails are mailto links on the Construction page (Thomas Petto: Tpetto@readington.gov; Kristina Chin: KChin@readington.gov; Jeanine Caruso: Jcaruso@readington.gov).

requirements: Smoke alarms as required for the year the home was built or renovated (for example, homes before 1977 need 10-year sealed battery alarms on all levels including the basement and within 10 feet outside all bedrooms; later homes must keep hardwired and interconnected alarms)
Hardwired smoke alarms may not be replaced with battery alarms; the most recent approved configuration must be kept
Carbon monoxide alarms within 10 feet outside every bedroom; battery or plug-in units allowed for homes built before 2016; alarms no older than 10 years
All alarms must be UL listed and replaced at end-of-life signal or 10 years from manufacture; smoke alarms at least 36 inches from ceiling fans and vents

Homes with a generator, solar panels, battery storage or other secondary power source need reflective 'CAUTION MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER' labels (ANSI Z535.4) within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and meter
House numbers at least 4 inches high, reflective or high-contrast, facing the access road
A fire alarm or combined burglar/fire alarm system that does not meet the listed requirements will not pass; finished basements are reported to the building department

authorities.name: Raritan Township Department of Fire Safety Services (Fire Marshal's Office)
authorities.area_served: Entire township (under a shared service agreement with Raritan Township)
authorities.lead_time: Fee depends on business days between receipt of the completed application and fee and the closing date: 11 or more business days for the lowest fee. Inspections are on Wednesdays. The Township page recommends applying a couple of weeks before closing and says the certificate is good for 90 days.

fees.label: Smoke alarm and CO alarm certificate, completed application and fee received 11 or more business days before closing
fees.quote: FEE: $55.00 ... When completed application and fee are received 11 or more BUSINESS days prior to closing date

fees.label: Received 10 or fewer and at least 4 business days before closing
fees.quote: FEE: $100.00 ... When completed application and fee are received 10 or less and up to 4 BUSINESS days prior to closing date

fees.label: Received less than 4 business days before closing
fees.quote: FEE: $160.00 ... When completed application and fee are received less than 4 BUSINESS days prior to closing date

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Township's SDL portal smoke detector application, or send the paper application with a check or money order payable to Raritan Township to the Department of Fire Safety Services, One Municipal Drive, Flemington, NJ 08822 (firesafety@raritantwpnj.gov). Fees must be paid before the certificate is issued. Inspections are done on Wednesdays; the office calls the Monday before with a time slot and takes no special requests.
authorities.contact_title: Chief Fire Marshal (administrative assistant Suanne Traynor, (908) 806-6100 ext. 2280)

fire_cert.notes: Readington's Fire Prevention page sends all inquiries to the Raritan Township Fire Safety office, and Readington Code Section 123-2 names the Raritan Township Department of Fire Safety as the local enforcing agency under a shared service agreement (July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2028). The current Raritan application (July 6, 2026) lists Readington and uses the $55 / $100 / $160 tiers. Readington's page still gives a local line, 908-534-4051 ext. 263, and fireofficial@readington.gov. The form and guide list no fire extinguisher.
